rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Consistency from the Ratios of Coefficients
rows.stem: The pair of linear equations \(x + 2y + 5 = 0\) and \(-3x = 6y - 1\) has
rows.solution:
Write the second equation as \(3x + 6y - 1 = 0\). Comparing with \(x + 2y + 5 = 0\):

\(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), \(\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), \(\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{5}{-1} = -5\).

\(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \neq \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), so the lines are parallel and the pair has no solution. This is option (D) no solution.

rows.stem: The common difference of the A.P. \(\dfrac{1}{2x}, \dfrac{1 - 4x}{2x}, \dfrac{1 - 8x}{2x}, \ldots\) is :
rows.solution:
\(d = \dfrac{1 - 4x}{2x} - \dfrac{1}{2x} = \dfrac{-4x}{2x} = -2\).

(The next difference is the same: \(\dfrac{1 - 8x}{2x} - \dfrac{1 - 4x}{2x} = \dfrac{-4x}{2x} = -2\).) This is option (B) \(-2\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: Two dice are thrown together. The probability that they show different numbers is :
rows.solution:
Two dice give 36 equally likely outcomes. The same number shows on both in 6 of them: (1, 1), (2, 2), ..., (6, 6).

\(P(\text{different numbers}) = 1 - \dfrac{6}{36} = \dfrac{5}{6}\), which is option (B) \(5/6\).

rows.stem: The probability of guessing the correct answer to a certain test question is \(\dfrac{x}{6}\). If the probability of not guessing the correct answer to this question is \(\dfrac{2}{3}\), then the value of \(x\) is :
rows.solution:
Guessing correctly and not guessing correctly are complementary events, so \(\dfrac{x}{6} + \dfrac{2}{3} = 1\).

\(\dfrac{x}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), so \(x = 2\), which is option (A) \(2\).

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: If \(a = 2^2 \times 3^x\), \(b = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5\), \(c = 2^2 \times 3 \times 7\) and LCM \((a, b, c) = 3780\), then \(x\) is equal to
rows.solution:
The LCM takes the highest power of each prime: LCM \((a, b, c) = 2^2 \times 3^m \times 5 \times 7 = 140 \times 3^m\), where m is the larger of x and 1.

\(140 \times 3^m = 3780\) gives \(3^m = 27 = 3^3\), so \(m = 3\). Since \(3 > 1\), the highest power of 3 comes from a, and \(x = 3\), which is option (C) \(3\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: The zeroes of the quadratic polynomial \(2x^2 - 3x - 9\) are :
From a point on the ground, which is 30 m away from the foot of a vertical tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is found to be \(60^\circ\). The height (in metres) of the tower is :
rows.solution:
Let h m be the height. Then \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{h}{30}\), so \(h = 30\sqrt{3}\).

The height is \(30\sqrt{3}\) m, which is option (B) \(30\sqrt{3}\).

rows.stem: If \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) and \(\sin\phi = \dfrac{1}{2}\), then \(\tan(\theta + \phi)\) is :
rows.solution:
\(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) gives \(\theta = 30^\circ\), and \(\sin\phi = \dfrac{1}{2}\) gives \(\phi = 30^\circ\) (both acute).

\(\tan(\theta + \phi) = \tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}\), which is option (A) \(\sqrt{3}\).

rows.stem: Maximum number of common tangents that can be drawn to two circles intersecting at two distinct points is :
rows.solution:
When two circles cut each other at two points, only the two direct common tangents can be drawn; a transverse common tangent would have to pass between the circles, which overlap.

So the maximum number is 2, which is option (C) \(2\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, if PT is a tangent to a circle with centre O and \(\angle TPO = 35^\circ\), then the measure of \(\angle x\) is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - which angle x is (at O, between OP and the radius TO produced through O to the far side of the circle) is fixed only by the drawing; the words do not define it. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
The radius OT is perpendicular to the tangent PT, so \(\angle OTP = 90^\circ\). In triangle OTP, \(\angle TOP = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 35^\circ = 55^\circ\).

In the figure, x is the angle at O between OP and TO produced beyond O. It forms a linear pair with \(\angle TOP\), so \(x = 180^\circ - 55^\circ = 125^\circ\). (Equally, x is the exterior angle of triangle OTP at O: \(x = 90^\circ + 35^\circ\).)

This is option (D) \(125^\circ\).

rows.stem: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral divide each other proportionally, then it is a :
rows.solution:
Let the diagonals AC and BD of quadrilateral ABCD meet at O with \(\dfrac{AO}{OC} = \dfrac{BO}{OD}\). Draw a line through O parallel to AB, meeting AD at E. By the Basic Proportionality Theorem in triangle DAB, \(\dfrac{AE}{ED} = \dfrac{BO}{OD} = \dfrac{AO}{OC}\), so by its converse in triangle ADC, \(EO \parallel DC\). Then \(AB \parallel DC\).

One pair of opposite sides is parallel, so the quadrilateral is a trapezium. This is option (D) trapezium.

rows.stem: In \(\Delta ABC\), \(DE \parallel BC\) (as shown in the figure). If AD = 2 cm, BD = 3 cm, BC = 7.5 cm, then the length of DE (in cm) is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that D lies on AB and E on AC is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
D lies on AB and E on AC, so \(AB = AD + DB = 2 + 3 = 5\) cm.

\(DE \parallel BC\) gives \(\Delta ADE \sim \Delta ABC\) (AA), so \(\dfrac{DE}{BC} = \dfrac{AD}{AB}\): \(DE = \dfrac{2}{5} \times 7.5 = 3\) cm.

This is option (B) \(3\).

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: Given HCF \((2520, 6600) = 40\), LCM \((2520, 6600) = 252 \times k\), then the value of k is :
rows.solution:
HCF \(\times\) LCM \(=\) product of the two numbers, so LCM \(= \dfrac{2520 \times 6600}{40} = 2520 \times 165 = 252 \times 1650\).

So \(k = 1650\), which is option (A) \(1650\).

rows.subtopic: Irrational Numbers and Proof by Contradiction
rows.stem: A pair of irrational numbers whose product is a rational number is :
rows.solution:
\(\sqrt{3}\) and \(\sqrt{27}\) are both irrational, and \(\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{27} = \sqrt{81} = 9\), which is rational.

(The pairs with \(\sqrt{16} = 4\), \(\sqrt{4} = 2\) or \(\sqrt{36} = 6\) contain rational numbers, and \(\sqrt{5} \times \sqrt{2} = \sqrt{10}\) is irrational.) This is option (C) \((\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{27})\).

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: If a digit is chosen at random from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9; then the probability that this digit is an odd prime number is :
rows.solution:
Of the 9 digits, the odd primes are 3, 5 and 7 (2 is prime but even).

\(P = \dfrac{3}{9} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), which is option (A) \(\dfrac{1}{3}\).

rows.stem: The mean of five observations is 15. If the mean of first three observations is 14 and that of the last three observations is 17, then the third observation is
rows.solution:
Sum of all five observations \(= 5 \times 15 = 75\). Sum of the first three \(= 3 \times 14 = 42\), and sum of the last three \(= 3 \times 17 = 51\).

Adding the first three and the last three counts the third observation twice: \(42 + 51 = 75 + x_3\), so \(x_3 = 93 - 75 = 18\).

This is option (C) \(18\).

rows.stem: Perimeter of a sector of a circle whose central angle is \(90^\circ\) and radius 7 cm is :
rows.solution:
Length of the arc \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 = 11\) cm.

Perimeter of the sector \(= 11 + 2 \times 7 = 25\) cm, which is option (D) 25 cm.

rows.stem: In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle. MN is the chord and the tangent ML at point M makes an angle of \(70^\circ\) with MN. The measure of \(\angle MON\) is :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - circle with centre O, chord MN, radii OM and ON, tangent at M with the 70 degree angle marked between ML and MN; the stem states everything, and the non-reflex angle MON is 140 degrees whichever side of MN the 70 degree angle sits. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
The radius OM is perpendicular to the tangent ML, so \(\angle OMN = 90^\circ - 70^\circ = 20^\circ\).

\(OM = ON\) (radii), so \(\angle ONM = 20^\circ\), and \(\angle MON = 180^\circ - 20^\circ - 20^\circ = 140^\circ\).

This is option (B) \(140^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The point which divides the line segment joining the points \(A(1, 2)\) and \(B(-1, 1)\) internally in the ratio 1 : 2 is \(\left(\dfrac{-1}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}\right)\)

**Reason (R) :** The coordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining the points \(A(x_1, y_1)\) and \(B(x_2, y_2)\) in the ratio \(m_1 : m_2\) are \(\left(\dfrac{m_1x_2 + m_2x_1}{m_1 + m_2}, \dfrac{m_1y_2 + m_2y_1}{m_1 + m_2}\right)\)
rows.context: Questions number 19 and 20 are Assertion and Reason based questions carrying 1 mark each. Two statements are given, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
By the section formula with \(m_1 : m_2 = 1 : 2\), \(A(1, 2)\) and \(B(-1, 1)\), the point is

\(\left(\dfrac{1 \times (-1) + 2 \times 1}{3}, \dfrac{1 \times 1 + 2 \times 2}{3}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}\right)\), not \(\left(\dfrac{-1}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}\right)\). The Assertion is false.

The Reason states the section formula correctly, so it is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** In a cricket match, a batsman hits a boundary 9 times out of 45 balls he plays. The probability that in a given ball, he does not hit the boundary is \(\dfrac{4}{5}\).

**Reason (R) :** \(P(E) + P(\text{not } E) = 1\)
rows.context: Questions number 19 and 20 are Assertion and Reason based questions carrying 1 mark each. Two statements are given, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
P(boundary) \(= \dfrac{9}{45} = \dfrac{1}{5}\), so P(no boundary) \(= 1 - \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{4}{5}\). The Assertion is true.

\(P(E) + P(\text{not } E) = 1\) is true, and it is exactly the rule used to get \(\dfrac{4}{5}\).

Both are true and the Reason is the correct explanation, which is option (A).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.solution:
There are 52 equally likely outcomes.

(i) There is one queen of hearts, so \(P(\text{queen of hearts}) = \dfrac{1}{52}\).

(ii) There are 4 jacks, so \(52 - 4 = 48\) cards are not jacks: \(P(\text{not a jack}) = \dfrac{48}{52} = \dfrac{12}{13}\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: If \(2x + y = 13\) and \(4x - y = 17\), find the value of \((x - y)\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: Sum of two numbers is 105 and their difference is 45. Find the numbers.
rows.solution:
Let the numbers be x and y, with \(x > y\).

\(x + y = 105\) ... (i)

\(x - y = 45\) ... (ii)

Adding, \(2x = 150\), so \(x = 75\), and \(y = 105 - 75 = 30\).

The numbers are 75 and 30.

rows.stem: Find a relation between \(x\) and \(y\) such that the point \(P(x, y)\) is equidistant from the points \(A(7, 1)\) and \(B(3, 5)\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: Points \(A(-1, y)\) and \(B(5, 7)\) lie on a circle with centre \(O(2, -3y)\) such that AB is a diameter of the circle. Find the value of \(y\). Also, find the radius of the circle.
rows.solution:
AB is a diameter, so the centre \(O(2, -3y)\) is the mid-point of AB.

Comparing ordinates: \(\dfrac{y + 7}{2} = -3y\), so \(y + 7 = -6y\) and \(y = -1\). (The abscissa checks: \(\dfrac{-1 + 5}{2} = 2\).)

The centre is \(O(2, 3)\), and the radius is \(OB = \sqrt{(5 - 2)^2 + (7 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5\) units.

rows.stem: In the given figure, \(\dfrac{EA}{EC} = \dfrac{EB}{ED}\), prove that \(\Delta EAB \sim \Delta ECD\)
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that AC and BD are straight lines crossing at E (A-E-C and B-E-D), which gives the vertically opposite angles at E, is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
In triangles EAB and ECD:

\(\dfrac{EA}{EC} = \dfrac{EB}{ED}\) (given), and \(\angle AEB = \angle CED\) (vertically opposite angles, since AC and BD cross at E).

So the sides including the equal angles are proportional, and by the SAS similarity criterion \(\Delta EAB \sim \Delta ECD\).

rows.stem: Evaluate : \(\dfrac{\cos 45^\circ + \sin 60^\circ}{\sec 30^\circ + \operatorname{cosec} 30^\circ}\).
rows.solution:
\(\dfrac{\cos 45^\circ + \sin 60^\circ}{\sec 30^\circ + \operatorname{cosec} 30^\circ} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} + 2}\)

The numerator is \(\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{6}}{2\sqrt{2}}\) and the denominator is \(\dfrac{2(1 + \sqrt{3})}{\sqrt{3}}\), so the value is

\(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}(2 + \sqrt{6})}{4\sqrt{2}(1 + \sqrt{3})} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{2}}{4\sqrt{2}(1 + \sqrt{3})}\).

This simplifies to \(\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{6}}{4(1 + \sqrt{3})} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{6} - 3}{8}\), any of these forms being acceptable.

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: If the sum of first 7 terms of an A.P. is 49 and that of first 17 terms is 289, find the sum of its first 20 terms.
rows.solution:
Let a be the first term and d the common difference.

\(S_7 = \dfrac{7}{2}(2a + 6d) = 49\), so \(a + 3d = 7\) ... (i)

\(S_{17} = \dfrac{17}{2}(2a + 16d) = 289\), so \(a + 8d = 17\) ... (ii)

Subtracting (i) from (ii): \(5d = 10\), so \(d = 2\), and then \(a = 1\).

\(S_{20} = \dfrac{20}{2}[2(1) + 19(2)] = 10 \times 40 = 400\).

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: The ratio of the \(10^{\text{th}}\) term to its \(30^{\text{th}}\) term of an A.P. is 1 : 3 and the sum of its first six terms is 42. Find the first term and the common difference of A.P.
rows.solution:
Let a be the first term and d the common difference.

\(\dfrac{a + 9d}{a + 29d} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), so \(3a + 27d = a + 29d\), giving \(2a = 2d\), that is \(a = d\) ... (i)

\(S_6 = \dfrac{6}{2}(2a + 5d) = 42\), so \(2a + 5d = 14\) ... (ii)

Substituting (i) in (ii): \(7a = 14\), so \(a = 2\) and \(d = 2\).

The first term is 2 and the common difference is 2.

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial \(x^2 - 15\) and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients of the polynomial.
rows.solution:
\(x^2 - 15 = (x - \sqrt{15})(x + \sqrt{15})\), so the zeroes are \(\sqrt{15}\) and \(-\sqrt{15}\).

Verification (here \(a = 1\), \(b = 0\), \(c = -15\)):

Sum of zeroes \(= \sqrt{15} + (-\sqrt{15}) = 0 = \dfrac{-0}{1} = \dfrac{-(\text{coefficient of } x)}{\text{coefficient of } x^2}\).

Product of zeroes \(= \sqrt{15} \times (-\sqrt{15}) = -15 = \dfrac{-15}{1} = \dfrac{\text{constant term}}{\text{coefficient of } x^2}\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem:
Solve the following system of linear equations graphically :

\(x - y + 1 = 0\)

\(x + y = 5\)
rows.solution:
For \(x - y + 1 = 0\), that is \(y = x + 1\):

| \(x\) | 0 | \(-1\) | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 1 | 0 | 3 |

For \(x + y = 5\), that is \(y = 5 - x\):

| \(x\) | 0 | 5 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 5 | 0 | 3 |

Graph: on one pair of axes, plot the points of each table and join them to draw the two lines, labelling each with its equation. The line \(x - y + 1 = 0\) rises through \((-1, 0)\) and \((0, 1)\); the line \(x + y = 5\) falls through \((0, 5)\) and \((5, 0)\).

The lines meet at \((2, 3)\), so the solution is \(x = 2\), \(y = 3\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: Find the ratio in which the line segment joining the points \((5, 3)\) and \((-1, 6)\) is divided by Y-axis.
rows.solution:
Every point on the y-axis has abscissa 0, so let the y-axis divide the segment joining \((5, 3)\) and \((-1, 6)\) at \((0, y)\) in the ratio \(k : 1\).

\(0 = \dfrac{k(-1) + 1(5)}{k + 1}\), so \(-k + 5 = 0\) and \(k = 5\).

The ratio is \(5 : 1\). (The point of division is \(\left(0, \dfrac{5 \times 6 + 3}{6}\right) = \left(0, \dfrac{11}{2}\right)\).)

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: \(P(-2, 5)\) and \(Q(3, 2)\) are two points. Find the coordinates of the point R on line segment PQ such that PR = 2QR.
rows.solution:
Let R be \((x, y)\). R lies on PQ with \(PR = 2QR\), so \(PR : RQ = 2 : 1\).

\(x = \dfrac{2(3) + 1(-2)}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{4}{3}\), \(y = \dfrac{2(2) + 1(5)}{2 + 1} = 3\).

The coordinates of R are \(\left(\dfrac{4}{3}, 3\right)\).

rows.stem: Prove that \(\dfrac{\sin\theta - 2\sin^3\theta}{2\cos^3\theta - \cos\theta} = \tan\theta\).
rows.solution:
LHS \(= \dfrac{\sin\theta - 2\sin^3\theta}{2\cos^3\theta - \cos\theta} = \dfrac{\sin\theta(1 - 2\sin^2\theta)}{\cos\theta(2\cos^2\theta - 1)}\)

\(= \dfrac{\tan\theta(1 - 2\sin^2\theta)}{2(1 - \sin^2\theta) - 1} = \dfrac{\tan\theta(1 - 2\sin^2\theta)}{1 - 2\sin^2\theta}\)

\(= \tan\theta =\) RHS.

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: Prove that the tangents drawn at the end points of a chord of a circle makes equal angles with the chord.
rows.solution:
Figure: a circle with centre O and a chord AB; the tangents at A and at B meet at a point P outside the circle.

The two tangents PA and PB are drawn from the same external point P, so \(PA = PB\).

In triangle PAB, the sides PA and PB are equal, so the angles opposite them are equal: \(\angle PBA = \angle PAB\).

So the tangents make equal angles with the chord AB.

(If AB is a diameter, the tangents at its ends are parallel and do not meet; each is perpendicular to AB, so both make an angle of \(90^\circ\) with it, and the angles are again equal.)

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: In a flight of 2800 km, an aircraft was slowed down due to bad weather. Its average speed is reduced by 100 km/h and by doing so, the time of flight is increased by 30 minutes. Find the original duration of the flight.
rows.solution:
Let the original speed be x km/h. The reduced speed is \((x - 100)\) km/h, and 30 minutes is \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) hour:

\(\dfrac{2800}{x - 100} - \dfrac{2800}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2}\)

\(\dfrac{2800 \times 100}{x(x - 100)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(x(x - 100) = 560000\), that is \(x^2 - 100x - 560000 = 0\).

\((x - 800)(x + 700) = 0\), so \(x = 800\) (a speed cannot be negative, so \(x \neq -700\)).

Original duration \(= \dfrac{2800}{800} = \dfrac{7}{2}\) hours, that is 3 hours 30 minutes.

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: The denominator of a fraction is one more than twice the numerator. If the sum of the fraction and its reciprocal is \(2\dfrac{16}{21}\), find the fraction.
rows.solution:
Let the numerator be x. Then the denominator is \(2x + 1\), and the fraction is \(\dfrac{x}{2x + 1}\).

\(\dfrac{x}{2x + 1} + \dfrac{2x + 1}{x} = 2\dfrac{16}{21} = \dfrac{58}{21}\)

\(21[x^2 + (2x + 1)^2] = 58x(2x + 1)\), so \(105x^2 + 84x + 21 = 116x^2 + 58x\), that is \(11x^2 - 26x - 21 = 0\).

\((x - 3)(11x + 7) = 0\), so \(x = 3\) (the numerator \(-\dfrac{7}{11}\) is not acceptable).

The fraction is \(\dfrac{3}{7}\). (Check: \(\dfrac{3}{7} + \dfrac{7}{3} = \dfrac{9 + 49}{21} = \dfrac{58}{21}\).)

rows.stem: State and prove Basic Proportionality theorem.
rows.solution:
Statement (Basic Proportionality Theorem): if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.

Given: in triangle ABC, a line parallel to BC meets AB at D and AC at E. To prove: \(\dfrac{AD}{DB} = \dfrac{AE}{EC}\).

Construction: join BE and CD, and draw \(DM \perp AC\) and \(EN \perp AB\).

Figure: triangle ABC with DE parallel to BC, D on AB and E on AC, and the segments BE, CD, DM and EN drawn.

Proof: \(\dfrac{\text{ar}(ADE)}{\text{ar}(BDE)} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{2} AD \cdot EN}{\frac{1}{2} DB \cdot EN} = \dfrac{AD}{DB}\), and \(\dfrac{\text{ar}(ADE)}{\text{ar}(DEC)} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{2} AE \cdot DM}{\frac{1}{2} EC \cdot DM} = \dfrac{AE}{EC}\).

Triangles BDE and DEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallels DE and BC, so \(\text{ar}(BDE) = \text{ar}(DEC)\). Hence \(\dfrac{AD}{DB} = \dfrac{AE}{EC}\).

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A solid iron pole consists of a solid cylinder of height 200 cm and base diameter 28 cm, which is surmounted by another cylinder of height 50 cm and radius 7 cm. Find the mass of the pole, given that 1 \(\text{cm}^3\) of iron has approximately 8 g mass.
rows.solution:
The lower cylinder has radius \(\dfrac{28}{2} = 14\) cm and height 200 cm; the upper cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 50 cm.

Volume of the pole \(= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 14 \times 200 + \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 \times 50 = 123200 + 7700 = 130900\) cm\(^3\).

Mass of the pole \(= 8 \times 130900 = 1047200\) g, that is 1047.2 kg.

rows.subtopic: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A medicine capsule is in the shape of a cylinder with two hemispheres stuck to each of its ends. The length of the entire capsule is 14 mm and the diameter of the capsule is 4 mm, find its surface area. Also, find its volume.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the capsule drawn as a cylinder with hemispherical ends, marked 4 mm (diameter) and 14 mm (overall length); both values are in the stem. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
The radius of each hemisphere equals the radius of the cylinder, \(\dfrac{4}{2} = 2\) mm. The length of the cylindrical part is \(14 - 2 - 2 = 10\) mm.

Surface area = CSA of the cylinder + 2 (CSA of a hemisphere)

\(= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2 \times 10 + 2 \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2 \times 2 = \dfrac{880}{7} + \dfrac{352}{7} = \dfrac{1232}{7} = 176\) mm\(^2\).

Volume = volume of the cylinder + 2 (volume of a hemisphere)

\(= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2 \times 2 \times 10 + 2 \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 = \dfrac{880}{7} + \dfrac{704}{21} = \dfrac{3344}{21} \approx 159.24\) mm\(^3\).

rows.stem: Find the area of the square shaped grass field.
rows.context:
A stable owner has four horses. He usually tie these horses with 7 m long rope to pegs at each corner of a square shaped grass field of 20 m length, to graze in his farm. But tying with rope sometimes results in injuries to his horses, so he decided to build fence around the area so that each horse can graze.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - a photo-diagram of the square field ABCD (20 m side) with a horse at each corner and the 7 m quadrant arcs; every value is in the passage. Page idx 20.
rows.solution: The field is a square of side 20 m, so its area is \(20 \times 20 = 400\) m\(^2\).

rows.stem: Find the area of the total field in which these horses can graze.
rows.context:
A stable owner has four horses. He usually tie these horses with 7 m long rope to pegs at each corner of a square shaped grass field of 20 m length, to graze in his farm. But tying with rope sometimes results in injuries to his horses, so he decided to build fence around the area so that each horse can graze.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the square field with the four 7 m quadrant arcs at the corners; every value is in the passage. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
Each horse is tied at a corner of the square with a 7 m rope, so it grazes a quadrant (a sector of angle \(90^\circ\)) of radius 7 m. The four quadrants together make one full circle:

Total area grazed \(= 4 \times \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 154\) m\(^2\).

rows.stem: If the length of the rope of each horse is increased from 7 m to 10 m, find the area grazed by one horse. (Use \(\pi = 3.14\))
rows.context:
A stable owner has four horses. He usually tie these horses with 7 m long rope to pegs at each corner of a square shaped grass field of 20 m length, to graze in his farm. But tying with rope sometimes results in injuries to his horses, so he decided to build fence around the area so that each horse can graze.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the square field with the four quadrant arcs at the corners; every value is in the passage and the stem. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
With a 10 m rope, one horse grazes a quadrant of radius 10 m:

Area \(= \dfrac{1}{4} \times 3.14 \times 10 \times 10 = 78.5\) m\(^2\).

rows.stem: What is area of the field that is left ungrazed, if the length of the rope of each horse is 7 cm ?
rows.context:
A stable owner has four horses. He usually tie these horses with 7 m long rope to pegs at each corner of a square shaped grass field of 20 m length, to graze in his farm. But tying with rope sometimes results in injuries to his horses, so he decided to build fence around the area so that each horse can graze.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the square field with the four 7 m quadrant arcs at the corners; every value is in the passage and the stem. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
Ungrazed area = area of the square field (\(20 \times 20 = 400\) m\(^2\)) minus the area the horses can graze.

With a 7 cm rope, each horse grazes a quadrant of radius 7 cm, and the four quadrants make one circle: \(4 \times \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 154\) cm\(^2\), which is 0.0154 m\(^2\).

Ungrazed area \(= 400 - 0.0154 = 399.9846\) m\(^2\).

The passage gives the rope as 7 m, so "7 cm" here is almost certainly a misprint; with a 7 m rope the grazed area is 154 m\(^2\) and the ungrazed area is \(400 - 154 = 246\) m\(^2\).

rows.stem: What is the lower limit of the modal class of the above data ?
rows.context:
Vocational training complements traditional education by providing practical skills and hands-on experience. While education equips individuals with a broad knowledge base, vocational training focuses on job-specific skills, enhancing employability thus making the student self-reliant. Keeping this in view, a teacher made the following table giving the frequency distribution of students/adults undergoing vocational training from the training institute.

| **Age (in years)** | 15-19 | 20-24 | 25-29 | 30-34 | 35-39 | 40-44 | 45-49 | 50-54 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Number of participants** | 62 | 132 | 96 | 37 | 13 | 11 | 10 | 4 |

From the above answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - a word-cloud image ('Education', 'Vocational', 'skill', ...); every number is in the table. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
The highest frequency is 132, for the age group 20-24, so that is the modal class.

The classes are not continuous, so subtract 0.5 from each lower limit and add 0.5 to each upper limit. The modal class becomes 19.5-24.5, and its lower limit is 19.5.

rows.stem: Find the median class of the above data.
rows.context:
Vocational training complements traditional education by providing practical skills and hands-on experience. While education equips individuals with a broad knowledge base, vocational training focuses on job-specific skills, enhancing employability thus making the student self-reliant. Keeping this in view, a teacher made the following table giving the frequency distribution of students/adults undergoing vocational training from the training institute.

| **Age (in years)** | 15-19 | 20-24 | 25-29 | 30-34 | 35-39 | 40-44 | 45-49 | 50-54 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Number of participants** | 62 | 132 | 96 | 37 | 13 | 11 | 10 | 4 |

From the above answer the following questions :
rows.solution:
Making the classes continuous and adding the cumulative frequencies:

| Age (in years) | 14.5-19.5 | 19.5-24.5 | 24.5-29.5 | 29.5-34.5 | 34.5-39.5 | 39.5-44.5 | 44.5-49.5 | 49.5-54.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of participants | 62 | 132 | 96 | 37 | 13 | 11 | 10 | 4 |
| cf | 62 | 194 | 290 | 327 | 340 | 351 | 361 | 365 |

\(N = 365\), so \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 182.5\). The first cumulative frequency above 182.5 is 194, so the median class is 19.5-24.5 (the age group 20-24).

rows.stem: Find the number of participants of age less than 50 years who undergo vocational training.
rows.context:
Vocational training complements traditional education by providing practical skills and hands-on experience. |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Number of participants** | 62 | 132 | 96 | 37 | 13 | 11 | 10 | 4 |

From the above answer the following questions :
rows.solution:
Participants of age less than 50 years are all those in the groups 15-19 to 45-49:

\(62 + 132 + 96 + 37 + 13 + 11 + 10 = 361\).

(Equally, it is the total 365 minus the 4 participants aged 50-54.)

rows.stem: What is the least prime number used by students ?
rows.context:
Teaching Mathematics through activities is a powerful approach that enhances students’ understanding and engagement. Keeping this in mind, Ms. Mukta planned a prime number game for class 5 students. She announces the number 2 in her class and asked the first student to multiply it by a prime number and then pass it to second student. Second student also multiplied it by a prime number and passed it to third student. In this way by multiplying to a prime number, the last student got 173250.

Now, Mukta asked some questions as given below to the students :
rows.solution:
\(173250 = 2 \times 3^2 \times 5^3 \times 7 \times 11\).

The 2 was announced by the teacher, and \(173250 \div 2 = 86625\) is odd, so no student multiplied by 2. The students used the primes 3, 3, 5, 5, 5, 7 and 11, and the least of these is 3.

rows.stem: How many students are in the class ?
rows.context:
Teaching Mathematics through activities is a powerful approach that enhances students’ understanding and engagement. Keeping this in mind, Ms. Mukta planned a prime number game for class 5 students. She announces the number 2 in her class and asked the first student to multiply it by a prime number and then pass it to second student. Second student also multiplied it by a prime number and passed it to third student. In this way by multiplying to a prime number, the last student got 173250.

Now, Mukta asked some questions as given below to the students :
rows.solution:
\(173250 = 2 \times 3^2 \times 5^3 \times 7 \times 11\). The 2 was the teacher's starting number, and each student multiplied by exactly one prime.

So the number of students is the number of prime factors after the 2: \(2 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 7\). There are 7 students in the class.

Now, Mukta asked some questions as given below to the students :
rows.solution:
\(173250 = 2 \times 3^2 \times 5^3 \times 7 \times 11\), and the students multiplied by 3, 3, 5, 5, 5, 7 and 11.

The highest prime number used by the students is 11.

rows.context:

So 5 has been used the maximum number of times.
